name: Thomas E Gottwald
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, NewMarket Corporation (NYSE: NEU), Richmond, Virginia
profile: Thomas E. 'Teddy' Gottwald is third-generation leader of the Gottwald family's Richmond chemicals business. He joined Ethyl in 1984, became NewMarket president/CEO in 2004 and chairman in 2014, succeeding his father Bruce. NewMarket owns Afton Chemical (petroleum additives) and in 2025 bought Calca Solutions, a maker of aerospace/defense propellants.
interesting_fact: His grandfather Floyd D. Gottwald Sr. ran Albemarle Paper, which in 1962 bought the much larger Ethyl Gasoline company, a famous early leveraged deal. Ethyl later became NewMarket.
deep_cut_fact: He is a Virginia Military Institute graduate and a former rector of VMI's Board of Visitors. He also chairs VMI's Jackson-Hope Board of Overseers.
notes: Low-profile CEO. Best route is NewMarket Corporate Communications in Richmond. The Calca propellants deal and the additives business are natural energy-podcast angles.

name: David E. Goel
current_role: Founder, Matrix Capital Management (Waltham, MA). He announced in 2024 that the fund would close and still holds large life-science stakes (Alumis, Aura Biosciences).
profile: Toronto-born, Harvard-educated 'Tiger Cub' investor. He trained under Julian Robertson at Tiger Management and founded Matrix Capital Management in 1999, running concentrated tech and life-science bets. Matrix led ACELYRIN's $250M Series B and anchored Alumis's 2024 IPO. ACELYRIN later merged into Alumis.
interesting_fact: He is one of Julian Robertson's 'Tiger Cubs'. He joined Tiger Management in 1996, became a partner, and started Matrix in 1999, a year before Tiger itself shut down.
deep_cut_fact: Before Tiger he started as a financial analyst in Morgan Stanley's high-technology investment banking group after Harvard (government, 1993). He then spent 1995-96 as an analyst at General Atlantic. He is also a 1989 Phillips Exeter graduate and has served on Exeter's board.
notes: Very private. No published personal or office contact found. He announced in August 2024 that he would wind down Matrix, citing personal reasons, so avoid that topic. Any approach would go through Matrix Capital or the boards of his portfolio companies.

name: Lin Jinxi
current_role: Founder, Chairman & General Manager, Changzhou Almaden Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 002623), a photovoltaic glass maker
profile: Lin Jinxi (林金锡) founded Changzhou Almaden in 2006. The company specialises in anti-reflective coated and ultra-thin photovoltaic glass for solar modules and supplies major panel makers such as JA Solar. He remains chairman and is taking Almaden overseas: in 2025 it announced a CNY 1.75B, 500,000-ton-per-year solar glass plant in the UAE.
interesting_fact: Almaden's planned UAE plant will make 1.6mm ultra-thin PV glass in the same industrial zone as Trina Solar's planned $5B Middle East manufacturing base.
deep_cut_fact: He is listed as an inventor on Almaden's own PV-glass patent filings. He is also vice president of the China New Energy Chamber of Commerce and of the Changzhou Photovoltaic Industry Association.
notes: Strong energy-podcast fit (solar supply chain, Middle East expansion). The company email is a general inbox. For a formal approach, use the board secretary listed in the SZSE annual report. The patent link rests on Justia records, which were not directly verified (blocked).

name: Luo Yun
current_role: Co-founder of Health and Happiness (H&H) International Holdings (HKEX: 1112), formerly Biostime. His current board role is not verified.
profile: Luo Yun (罗云) co-founded Biostime in Guangzhou in 1999 with Luo Fei, who is H&H's chairman and CEO. The company began with children's probiotics, then grew into infant formula and nutrition, and listed in Hong Kong in 2010. After buying 83% of Australia's Swisse Wellness in 2015 for A$1.45B it renamed itself H&H in 2017. Today it is a global nutrition group with brands including Swisse, Biostime and Good Goût.
interesting_fact: The 2015 Swisse purchase (A$1.45B for 83%) turned a Guangzhou infant-probiotics firm into the owner of one of Australia's best-known vitamin brands. It was among the largest Chinese takeovers of an Australian consumer brand.
deep_cut_fact: In 2013 Biostime took a 20% stake in Isigny Sainte Mère, a historic French Normandy dairy producer, to secure infant-formula supply. This was years before the Swisse deal.
